title: Quick Heal Technologies Ltd - 539678 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Quick Heal's Q2 FY27 revenue of INR 65 crore rose 44% QoQ but fell 22% YoY, with no numeric guidance given and a shift toward enterprise (around 56% of revenue) while consumer shrinks.

summary.headline: Quick Heal Q2 FY27 revenue rose 44% QoQ to INR 65 crore, with EBITDA turning positive at INR 2.3 crore, though revenue fell 22% YoY.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 was INR 65 crore, up 44% QoQ but down 22% YoY, with growth visible in both enterprise and consumer. Total expenditure excluding depreciation was flat QoQ at INR 63 crore, so EBITDA moved from a loss of INR 17.6 crore in Q1 to a profit of INR 2.3 crore, and PAT was INR 5.8 crore (9% margin). Receivables fell to INR 98 crore from INR 107 crore in Q1 and INR 176 crore a year earlier, and the company says it remains debt-free. Management reiterated its enterprise pivot and declined to give revenue or margin guidance.

segments.name: Enterprise (Seqrite)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 35 crore, up 18% QoQ and down 4% YoY; the company cites wins in defence, BFSI and a large IT services firm via new-generation products. Enterprise was about 56% of revenue per Dr. Katkar, though the same answer also says it is almost 50%.

segments.name: Consumer (Quick Heal)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 36 crore, up 86% QoQ but down 40% YoY; management tightened credit and commercial controls, which may moderate near-term volume.

guidance_outlook: No revenue, margin or cost guidance given; management said it does not provide guidance.
Management expects enterprise to exceed 80% of revenue within about three years, per Dr. Katkar's comment on the call.
Employee cost fell about INR 17 crore YoY; management said the cost base is now in a similar range and it will keep investing in R&D and sales where gaps exist.
International: stay selective, focused on Italy, Philippines and South America, with a few meaningful positions rather than broad spread.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or utilisation figures were discussed on the call.
Enterprise portfolio expanding into data privacy (DPDP-linked), exposure management and ransomware resilience; data privacy offering launched in the prior year.
Company is present in 70+ countries; no domestic vs international revenue split is reported.
demand_pricing: Consumer antivirus demand is structurally declining, which management attributes to Microsoft making free versions default and removing expired versions by default; management sees no consumer demand uplift from AI-driven attacks in the short term.
Enterprise targeting is small, medium and micro businesses in endpoint security, EDR, XDR and DLP; very large enterprises are excluded.
Management sees SMB cybersecurity spend rising as AI-driven attacks grow in sophistication.
Management does not give out revenue potential for individual products, but said DPDP is a significant medium-to-long-term driver and expects it to match endpoint security soon.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue and margin does management aspire to over the next three to four years?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Katkar declined to give revenue or margin outlook, saying the company does not disclose it, but said enterprise will exceed 80% of revenue within about three years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the biggest challenge in the business, and what external environment is needed for consistent growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Katkar named Microsoft's OS policies (default free antivirus, removal of expired versions) as the main consumer headwind; enterprise is fragmented, and the company targets SMB and mid-market rather than large enterprises.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue could DPDP-related products generate?
qa_highlights.answer: Harish Kumar did not quantify it, saying it is early, but described DPDP as a significant medium-to-long-term driver for enterprise.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost fall about INR 17 crore YoY, and is this a new run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Ankit Maheshwari said costs are being continuously optimised while R&D and sales investments are maintained; no run-rate guidance was given, and the cost base is in a similar range now.

qa_highlights.question: Does AI-driven threat growth create consumer tailwinds?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Katkar saw no consumer demand change unless a targeted attack hits individuals, which he does not expect in the short term; AI-led attacks are raising awareness in enterprises and mid-market.

qa_highlights.question: Split of revenue between international and Indian clients, and international expansion plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Harish Kumar said the domestic vs international split is not reported currently; international remains important with a selective, geography-focused approach.

risks_watch: Consumer revenue is down 40% YoY and management is tightening credit, which may moderate near-term consumer volume.
Platform dependence: Microsoft's default-antivirus policies are cited as the biggest consumer headwind.
Enterprise revenue is still down 4% YoY; the order book (above INR 57 crore) and enterprise share of revenue need to keep rising.
Q2 profitability relies on lower costs and a QoQ revenue rebound; sustainability of the positive EBITDA is not confirmed.
Management did not disclose domestic vs international revenue split and gave no guidance, limiting visibility.
summary.management_tone: Cautious and somewhat evasive on forward numbers: management declined to give revenue, margin or cost guidance and deferred several questions, while being confident on the enterprise strategy and the Q2 sequential recovery.
key_quotes: Our immediate priority is commercial execution.
We would rather build meaningful positions in a smaller number of markets than spread our resources too thin.
This may moderate some near-term volume, but we believe it is the right trade-off to improve receivables quality, channel discipline, and the economics of the business.
